Status: mode-only handoff. Substantive review (Sections 1–11, outputs, report) not yet run, per user request.

## Context

Working plan under review: `PLAN.md` (draft "deterministic skill-list ordering"). Users compare
skill listings in scripts and reviews, so enumeration-order noise shows up as spurious diffs.
The draft sorts registered skill names deterministically before rendering, holds membership,
aliases, metadata and text/JSON formats unchanged, and adds tests for mixed-case names and
differing directory enumeration order.

## Pre-review system audit

- Repo contains only `PLAN.md` and `CLAUDE.md` (single commit "Seed review plan"). The target
  listing code is not in this checkout; code-level leverage (0B) must be verified against the
  real codebase before the substantive review.
- No remote `origin`; base branch resolved to `main` via `origin/main` ref check fallback.
- No stashes, no TODO/FIXME markers, no `TODOS.md`, no design doc for `main`.

- Retrospective check: no prior reviews or reverts on record.
- DESIGN_SCOPE: none (CLI/library output ordering only; Section 11 skip expected).

## Landscape check (Layer 1/2/3)

- Layer 1: treat `readdir` order as random; sort explicitly, at the source, every level.
- Layer 2: reproducible-builds literature catalogs filesystem ordering as a standard
  nondeterminism source; recommends locale-independent (byte/codepoint) sort keys and testing
  under deliberately shuffled enumeration (disorderfs / reprotest pattern).
- Layer 3: sorting only the final render leaves intermediate behaviour (error messages, alias
  resolution, duplicate detection) order-dependent. The review should ask whether sorting
  belongs at registration rather than at render.

## Step 0 evidence

- 0A Premise: real problem is diff noise in scripted/reviewed listings; do-nothing cost is
  flaky comparisons and false "changed" signals. Plan addresses the pain directly.
- 0B Leverage: reuse the existing listing path; sort before render. Code not present here to
  confirm; implementation owner must identify the enumeration site.
- 0C Dream state: all user-facing listings stable and comparable across machines and runs.
  This plan moves toward it for one command.
- 0D: no required approach choice.

## Mode selection (0E)

- Estimated changed files: 2–3 (listing module + test file(s)); estimate.
- Category: fix/refactor → recommendation HOLD SCOPE.
- Resolution: `gstack-question-preference --check plan-ceo-review-mode` → AUTO_DECIDE (exit 0).
- Selected mode: **HOLD SCOPE**. Provenance: successful preference check; logged
  `plan-ceo-review-mode`, user_choice=HOLD SCOPE, recommended=HOLD SCOPE, auto_decided=true.
- Handoff sent in chat before tool calls.

| ID and owner | Contract and evidence | Current | Proposed | Status | Exact approval and scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (none yet) | | | | | |

Mode selection is an admin question; no ledger row. No plan changes approved.

- Prerequisite `/office-hours` offer: user handles separately.
- `routing-injection` onboarding block from skill-start: requires CLAUDE.md edit + commit;
  blocked by plan mode and deferred by user. Marker-based; will re-fire on next healthy run.
- Remaining HOLD SCOPE route: 0G (complexity check, minimum changes, invariants) → 0I → Review
  Sections 1–10 (11 skip) → outputs → `## GSTACK REVIEW REPORT`.

## Open items to raise in the substantive review

- Collation: case-insensitive vs byte order for mixed-case names; tie-break when two names
  differ only by case; locale independence.
- Alias placement relative to canonical names in text and JSON output.
- Where the sort lives (registration vs render) and whether error/log paths stay order-dependent.
- Test design for "differing directory enumeration order": inject a shuffled/reversed listing
  rather than depending on a real filesystem.
